# Grid: an opt-in row-geometry model drives offsets, extents and navigation

## Context

This is leaf L1 of epic #19658 (content-sized rows), graduated from D#19645. It replaces fixed-height arithmetic with one per-view geometry model, opt-in, before any measurement exists. Heights enter through an internal setter that tests drive directly, so geometry correctness can be proved in isolation. Measurement leaves L2 and L3 feed the same setter later.

## The Problem

Every row-position consumer multiplies or divides by one `rowHeight` (dev `bf91293bde`):
- **`Body`:** pool rows (L413), start index (L475), `scrollToIndex` (L1408–1411), extent (L1634).
- **`Row`:** height and transform (L399–400).
- **`View.syncBodies`:** start index (L380).
- **`VerticalScrollbar`:** extent (L152).

Variable heights break all of them at once. The two extents must also agree: `Body` and the proxy scrollbar write their extents independently today.

## The Architectural Reality

The App Worker owns geometry, and the three bodies (start, center, end) of one view share each row's height. `GridRowScrollPinning` reads scroll-origin deltas, not row heights (L117 and L159), and is unaffected here; L4 handles corrections.

## The Fix

- **Opt-in mode** on `grid.Container`, propagated to its bodies. Fixed height stays the default, and its arithmetic is untouched.
- **The geometry model, per view:**
  - a record-id-keyed height map, with the configured `rowHeight` as the estimate for unknown rows (the measured mean replaces it in L3);
  - a `Float64Array` of prefix offsets, rebuilt once per batch of height changes;
  - binary-search offset → row lookup.
- **Consumers in this mode** take it: `Row` offset and height, `View.syncBodies`, pixel-based pool coverage (viewport plus overscan, capped by row count, with the smallest known height as the floor), both extents, and `Body.scrollToIndex`.
- **One internal setter** (record id → px) applies heights and rebuilds offsets. There is no public height callback: consumer sizing policies stay deferred per D#19645.
- **The viewport height** that pixel coverage and keyboard alignment measure against is the view's own layout height (`Container.passSizeToBody`). *(Amended during implementation, see below.)*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] With the mode off, every existing grid spec passes unchanged; that is the fixed-height control.
- [x] With the mode on and synthetic mixed heights, row transforms, both extents (`Body` and `VerticalScrollbar`) and the start index all agree with the prefix offsets.
- [x] `scrollToIndex` reaches the right row, including the final row, which is reachable and fully visible.
- [x] Keyboard scrolling brings the target row fully into the view in both modes.
- [x] The three bodies of one view share each row's height, and two views at different widths keep independent models.
- [x] A sort or filter rebuilds the ordered offsets; the rebuild cost at 100k rows is measured and recorded in the PR.
- [x] New and changed methods carry JSDoc.

## Amendment (implementation finding)

The browser e2e for "the final row is fully visible" failed in both modes, so the cause is not row geometry. `Container.passSizeToBody` derived `availableHeight` as container − header − footer, which also counted the container borders and the horizontal scrollbar below the view: 770px against a 751px view in the fixture. Keyboard scrolling aligns a row's bottom with `availableHeight`, so the row ended 19px out of sight. That was reproduced on the fixed-height `grid-focus` grid (rows 12+ clipped by 19px). The derivation dates from #6184 (Jan 2025) and predates the in-flow horizontal scrollbar. Measuring the view itself fixes both modes, and this leaf's AC cannot pass without it, so it is in scope here rather than split out.

## Out of Scope

Measuring content (L2, L3), scroll correction with pinning (L4), `AnimateRows` (L5), and the example plus e2e journey (L6).

## Avoided Traps

- A Fenwick tree: the plain prefix array rebuilds 100k rows in about 0.07 ms (D#19645 probe 5).
- A public row-height callback: deferred.
- Changing the fixed-height arithmetic. The viewport measurement both modes share is the one exception, per the amendment.

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-10-12T14:17:54Z

**Intake: self-authored this session; stage 2 (prescription) is answered here.**

Prescription checked: `src/grid/View.mjs` owns the concern. The ticket said "one geometry model per view" without naming its owner. `grid.View` orchestrates the one to three bodies (`bodyStart`, `body`, `bodyEnd`), owns `scrollTop`, and computes the start index in `syncBodies` (L375–380). It already owns the grid's single selection model, keyed by record id across all bodies. Neither `Body` (one per region) nor `Container` (the macro layer) is the right owner.

Structural pre-flight, sibling-pattern fast path: the model's data structure goes in `src/grid/RowGeometry.mjs`, `Neo.grid.RowGeometry extends Neo.core.Base`. This mirrors `Neo.grid.ScrollManager`, a `core.Base` helper beside the grid components that its owner creates as a module. `grid.View` creates it only when content-sized mode is on. It holds the record-keyed heights, the `Float64Array` prefix offsets and the inverse lookup, and is unit-testable without a component tree.

Accretion note: this adds engine lines without deleting consumer lines, because it is a new opt-in capability and the fixed-height path must stay byte-for-byte. No simplification is claimed.

Files: `src/grid/{RowGeometry (new), View, Body, Row, VerticalScrollbar}.mjs`, `src/grid/Container.mjs` (the opt-in config only), and unit specs. They were announced to #19515 and #19643 in the claim broadcast.

- An order change (sort, filter, load, mutation, new estimate) runs the full

- The full pass reads store.items, since getAt() hydrates every lazy record.
- The geometry's store listeners run before the bodies' own (order: 'before'),
  so a body re-rendering on the store's load reads fresh offsets.
- A row finds its moved geometry itself (Row#hasStaleGeometry) and re-renders
  with cell recycling instead of a forced full render.
- Content-sized mode re-syncs on every new start row and sizes the pool by the
  smallest row height, so mixed heights never mount more rows than the pool.
- passSizeToBody measures the view. Container minus header also counted the
  borders and the horizontal scrollbar, which left a row that keyboard
  scrolling aligns to the bottom 19px out of sight, in fixed-height grids too.

* feat(grid): content-sized rows measure the wrapped text of wrapText columns (#19662)

In content-sized mode a wrapText column renders its text in a block container
(min-width: 0, so a word longer than the column breaks inside the cell). After
an update of the view, a body or a row lands, View#measureRowHeights reads the
layout boxes of the new containers of all bodies in one batch, adds the cell's
padding and borders, and gives each row its tallest column, never less than
rowHeight.

- Fence: a reply only counts for a cell node its row still renders at the
  width it was read at. A re-render (another record, new content, a new width)
  makes a new node, so the read for the old one is dropped.
- Measured nodes are not read again, so scrolling over measured rows reads
  nothing. Heights are kept per column, so a column scrolled out of the
  mounted range keeps its share of the row.
- Row.setCellId moves a text container's id along with its recycled cell.
- Turning wrapText on or off forgets the measured heights (resetRowHeights).

* fix(grid): a buffered resize after destroy reads no view; class hierarchy lists RowGeometry (#19661)

passSizeToBody now measures the view, and the buffered onResize can reach a
destroyed grid, whose view is null: SplitterHeavyContent's cadence arm got a
pageerror from it (3/3 locally without this). passSizeToBody returns when the
view is gone, and onResize stops after its await once the grid is destroyed.

* fix(grid): a replaced store's records start from the estimate, not the old store's heights (#19661)

RowGeometry kept its record-id-keyed heights when the view handed it another
store. With natural keys (useInternalId: false), a different record under a
repeated id then took the old store's height and offset. Heights still
outlive a sort or filter of their store; a new store clears them.

* fix(grid): a replaced store forgets the measured texts of the old store's records (#19662)

Same defect class as #19668's review RA-1: the view's per-column text heights
are keyed by record id, so a new record under a repeated natural id combined
its measured texts with the old record's. bindStore clears them, and the
measured-cell registry, when the store is replaced.

* test(grid): the measurement fence drops replies for recycled slots and changed widths (#19662)

#19662 AC-3 names three cases; the spec covered the content change only. Two
arms hold the read in flight: one recycles every pooled slot to other records,
one changes a recycled cell's width in place. Each fails with its fence
condition removed.

* fix(grid): measured row heights follow hidden cells, removed columns and rowHeight (#19662)

- A cell hidden with display none has no layout box. It is not read, and a reply whose box has no width
  is not kept, so the cell is measured once it shows, also at its unchanged width.
- When a wrapText column leaves the grid, the measured rows drop its text heights and derive their
  heights from the remaining columns, scrolled-out rows included.
- A new rowHeight derives the measured rows again from their stored text heights, so the floor applies
  in both directions."
